title: Balanced K-Factor Decomposition
summary: Given the integers n and k , decompose n into exactly k positive integers such that the product of these integers equals n .
statement: Given the integers n and k , decompose n into exactly k positive integers such that the product of these integers equals n . Return one such decomposition where the maximum difference between any two numbers in the decomposition is minimized, and the order of the numbers does not matter.
constraints: Four <= n <= 100,000 and two <= k <= five.
Return exactly k positive integers with product n.
Minimize maximum minus minimum; output order does not matter.
hints: An unordered decomposition has one nondecreasing representation.
Backtrack nondecreasing divisors and keep the tuple with smallest final-first spread.
At each slot try divisors no larger than the remaining product’s slots-th root, then place the final cofactor.
Every nondecreasing factorization follows exactly one branch; the root bound cannot exclude its next factor, and direct comparison selects the optimum.
editorial: Every nondecreasing factorization follows exactly one branch; the root bound cannot exclude its next factor, and direct comparison selects the optimum.

tests.explanation: Ten and ten multiply to one hundred with zero spread.
Two, two, and eleven give the minimum spread nine.
